title: A Song Gone Quiet
summary: Ribbit villages are never quiet. This one is. Somebody here should be playing something.

goals.say: She pats your hand with a cold, damp, very kind one. 'Go and find Bufo. He'll be glad of the company, though he won't say so.'
goals.name: Grandmother Pondwhistle

threats.name: Grandmother Pondwhistle
threats.target_line: Oh. A visitor. Mind the lily pads, dear, they're older than you are.
talk: Because the band has nothing to keep time to, dear. Somebody stole our music. Well. Our maraca. Same thing, to a frog.
The Golden Maraca. Every Ribbit band keeps the beat on one, and ours is the oldest in the swamp. Without it the others won't play. We are very particular about rhythm. Ribbit. Excuse me.
The Bog Hag. She lives in the hut on the stilts, past the cattails. She says our music curdles her potions. We say her potions curdle everything.
Bufo will tell you. He leads the band, when there is a band. He's been sulking under a lily pad since Tuesday.
